name: Should I replace cabinets or reface them?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to replace kitchen cabinets or reface them during a remodel?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to replace kitchen cabinets or reface them during a remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinet replacement and cabinet refacing solve different problems. Refacing keeps the existing cabinet boxes and updates the visible surfaces, which can be a smart move if the structure is sound and the layout already works. Replacement is better when the boxes are damaged, the storage is inefficient, or you want deeper drawers, taller uppers, better pantry solutions, or a completely different style. In Los Angeles remodels, many homeowners choose replacement because they are already investing in countertops, flooring, and appliances, and they want the kitchen to feel fully renewed. Refacing can be a good cost-saving option, but it makes the most sense when the current footprint is functional and the boxes are in excellent condition. A contractor should inspect the cabinetry before recommending either path.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace cabinets when the boxes are damaged, the layout is poor, or you want major storage improvements. Reface cabinets when the cabinet boxes are still solid and you only want a new look. Refacing is usually cheaper, but it offers fewer design changes than replacement.
